rome-at-war-series.specific_finding: The summary says attackers and defenders compare combat strengths, apply modifiers and consult a combat-results table. The publisher’s original Rome at War Learn to Play sheet, page1 Attacking, instead gives each unit a number of dice equal to its combat strength; each6scores a hit, with specified situations hitting on5or6. High morale and the highest-ranking leader can add dice. Page2 resolves ordinary assault rolls simultaneously, with specific missile-fire exceptions. Replacing this strength-sized hit-counting system with a strength-comparison CRT changes the core combat procedure. Specific MAJOR against the covered original publisher teaching sheet; full scenario/terrain/victory rules and exact2015ThirdEdition equivalence remain uncertified. No full audit or summary body repair.
